methods.label: Convert to an ordinary quadratic equation
methods.explanation:
The definition of a base-ten logarithm lets us remove the logarithm: its argument must equal \(10^2\). Thus
\[
\log_{10}(a^2-15a)=2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
a^2-15a=100.
\]
Moving everything to one side gives
\[
a^2-15a-100=0.
\]
The numbers \(-20\) and \(5\) have product \(-100\) and sum \(-15\), so
\[
(a-20)(a+5)=0.
\]
A product is zero only when one of its factors is zero. Hence \(a=20\) or \(a=-5\).

A real logarithm requires a positive argument. For either value, \(a^2-15a=100>0\), and \(\log_{10}100=2\), so both satisfy the original equation. The values are \(20\) and \(-5\), choice B.
